title: First and last booking for a room
prompt:
nums lists room numbers of bookings sorted in nondecreasing order; return [first, last], the first and last index where target appears, or [-1, -1] if it never does.

- nums has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^9 and 10^9; target is in the same range.
- Use O(log n) time, even when target appears many times.
- Return a list of two 0-based indices.
hints: Finding one copy and walking outward is O(n) when every value is target. Can you search for each end directly?
The first index is the lower bound: the first position whose value is >= target.
The last index is one less than the first position whose value is > target (the lower bound of target + 1). Check that the first position actually holds target.

solution.explanation: A lower-bound search finds the first index whose value is not less than x. The first occurrence is the lower bound of target, and the last occurrence sits just before the lower bound of the next larger value; if the first lower bound is not target, it is absent.

complexity.notes: Two independent lower-bound searches; Python's bisect_left and bisect_right are exactly these.

followUps: Count how many values fall in [lo, hi] in O(log n).
Do it with a single binary search helper parameterised by a predicate.
